subject: Renewal accelerator: usage fingerprint & surge risk
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novaworks.com>, Marco D'Souza <marco.dsouza@novaworks.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal accelerator: usage fingerprint & surge risk

Hi Elena / Marco —

Quick proactive note as we approach your Oct renewal: we've pulled a short usage fingerprint for NovaWorks covering Q2–Q3. A few highlights:

- Token mix shift: 38% of monthly tokens are from high-frequency inference (chat endpoints) vs 26% at the start of Q2.
- Burst exposure: two spikes (7/6 and 7/19) where sustained 95th-percentile TPS pushed latency > 400ms for 8–12 minutes.
- Cost/ROI: Chat features driving 3.6x higher end-user conversions on trials where latency < 250ms; when latency spikes, conversion drops ~18%.

I attached the csv and a short compendium to this thread. Before the renewal, we'd like to propose a short 30-minute review to:
1) walk the usage fingerprint
2) discuss a staged commit uplift + burst buffer to cover peak windows
3) review a mutual action plan that accelerates onboarding of the latency-sensitive features (we think a 20% capacity uplift + prefix caching will smooth spikes while keeping unit cost down).

Proposed times: Tue 7/26 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 7/28 14:00–14:30 PT. If you prefer, loop in procurement and we can surface a short MAP and draft amendment.

Attachments: redwood_q2_usage_fingerprint.csv, MAP_NovaWorks_v2.docx

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novaworks.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco D'Souza <marco.dsouza@novaworks.com>, procurement@novaworks.com
Date: 2028-07-25T08:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal accelerator: usage fingerprint & surge risk

Jordan —

Thanks for the snapshot, that timing works. We saw the same spikes on our side tied to an internal experiment rollout (variant B). A couple quick questions before we sync:

- Can you quantify expected unit cost delta for a 20% commit uplift vs current pay-as-you-go?
- Do you have a suggested SLA for the burst buffer? We need a clear escalation path when latency exceeds thresholds.
- Procurement is copied (procurement@novaworks.com) — would appreciate a short redline-ready MAP and the draft amendment so procurement can triage.

We prefer Thu 7/28 14:00 PT.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director of Product, NovaWorks
elena.ruiz@novaworks.com

Elena / team —

Appreciate the quick reply. Short answers to your questions ahead of the Thu call:

- Unit cost delta: a staged 20% commit uplift (12-month) we modeled reduces token unit cost by ~14% given your current token mix; with prefix caching we see an incremental 6–8% reduction on chat-heavy endpoints. I'll bring a two-scenario worksheet to the call (conservative and aggressive).

- Burst buffer & SLA: recommended burst buffer = 1.5x baseline sustained capacity for scheduled experiments; we can offer a 99.5% availability SLO on dedicated tranche + escalation contact and 15-minute paging for P1 incidents. For contract language we suggest a 4-hour remediation objective and 30-day credit cap in the MAP (we can tune per procurement).

- MAP & amendment: attached latency_snapshot_2028-07-22.pdf and an internal redline of MAP_NovaWorks_v2.docx. Also looping Hannah for exec-level approvals/redline support.

See you Thu 7/28 14:00 PT — invite sent.

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0333

Attachments: latency_snapshot_2028-07-22.pdf

Elena / Marco / Procurement —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and agreed next steps:

1) Commit uplift: NovaWorks to consider a staged 20% commit for first 6 months, with a re-eval at month 4. Kimberly will send the two-scenario worksheet and the cost delta table by EOD.
2) Burst buffer and SLA: Redwood provides a burst tranche (1.5x) and 99.5% availability SLO. Procurement to review the suggested 4-hour remediation objective and 30-day credit cap.
3) MAP & amendment: I uploaded the mutual action plan and the draft amendment here: https://docs.redwood.ai/shared/MAP-NovaWorks-v2. Procurement, if comfortable, we can route the draft for an e-signature approval — DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/na/document/preview/abc123
4) Technical follow-up: Hannah's team will run a short prefix-caching pilot on the staging bucket next week (Hannah copied).

Attachments: MAP_NovaWorks_v2.docx (final draft), redwood_q2_usage_fingerprint.csv

If procurement can confirm by Mon 8/5, Jordan/Redwood can prepare a contract amendment and an ops runbook for the pilot.

Jordan Blake
